[`bun test --aot`](/bundler/executables#try-your-code-without-building-an-executable) runs your tests under the rules of `bun build --compile --aot`. There the objects that JavaScript itself provides, such as `Math`, `Date` and `Array.prototype`, are immutable. A stub that is written in JavaScript replaces the original function with `Object.defineProperty()` or an assignment, so `sinon.stub(Math, "random")` throws a `TypeError` and the test fails. `spyOn()` of `bun:test` is part of the test runner and works on built-in objects too.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/aot-spy-on-builtin" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
import { mock } from "node:test";

mock.method(JSON, "parse", () => ({}));
mock.getter(Map.prototype, "size", () => 0);
```

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```js
import sinon from "sinon";

sinon.stub(Date, "now").returns(0);
sinon.spy(Object, "keys");
sinon.replace(Math, "random", () => 0.5);
```

Fake timers that are written in JavaScript replace the global `Date`:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```js
import FakeTimers from "@sinonjs/fake-timers";
import { mock } from "node:test";
import sinon from "sinon";

sinon.useFakeTimers();
FakeTimers.install({ now: 0 });
mock.timers.enable();
```

Not reported:

The spies of `bun:test`:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { jest, spyOn, vi } from "bun:test";

spyOn(Math, "random").mockReturnValue(0.5);
jest.spyOn(Date, "now").mockReturnValue(0);
vi.spyOn(Array.prototype, "push");
```

The fake timers of `bun:test` are part of Bun and replace nothing. They work under `--aot`, and `Date.now()` and `new Date()` follow them.

{/* good */}
```ts
import { jest, setSystemTime } from "bun:test";

setSystemTime(new Date("2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"));
jest.useFakeTimers();
jest.advanceTimersByTime(1000);
```

Fake timers that leave `Date` alone:

{/* good */}
```js
import { mock } from "node:test";
import sinon from "sinon";

sinon.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["setTimeout", "clearTimeout"] });
mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout"] });
```

What Bun adds to JavaScript stays mutable:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { spyOn } from "bun:test";

spyOn(console, "log");
spyOn(process, "cwd");
spyOn(performance, "now");
spyOn(globalThis, "fetch");
```

For anything else, let the code take the function that it calls, and pass another one in the test:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

function pick<T>(items: T[], random = Math.random): T {
  return items[Math.floor(random() * items.length)];
}

test("picks the first item", () => {
  expect(pick(["a", "b"], () => 0)).toBe("a");
});
```

## What it doesn't find

The rule only looks at calls in which the built-in object and the name of the property are written out: not `sinon.stub(target, name)`.
